single-latest-quarter.notes: B provides full QoQ/YoY analysis, accurate multi-quarter GM trajectory (noting 74.4% remains below early FY25's 78.4%/75.1%), operating leverage, segment concentration, and the 7-month staleness flag, lacking only source links. A links Q4 FY26 and FY26 figures cleanly but omits QoQ direction and analytical takeaways.

segment-drill-down.notes: A reports the exact Q4 FY26 segment split (Data Center $55.2B / 88.9%), highlights concentration risk, and flags single-quarter and post-Jan 2026 limits, lacking only source links. peer-two.notes: A links every FY26/FY25 figure cleanly and adds a sharp counterpoint that AMD's NI ($4.2B) exceeding OI ($3.4B) makes net margin overstate operating profitability, but omits growth rates and quarterly trajectories. B covers growth, margin trends, one-off shocks, mix, and price-data flaws while explicitly flagging the 5-month latest-quarter gap, lacking only source links.

cause-in-evidence.notes: A quotes AMD's 2025-08-05 8-K attribution of ~$800M MI308 export-control charges, quantifies the add-back (~8.7% OM) and +$264M OpEx increase, and shows the Q3-Q2 FY26 recovery (table figures lack source links). B links Q2 figures cleanly but falls into the trap of saying the data does not explain why the operating loss happened.

ticker-page-compare.notes: Both identify AAPL as primary, add NVDA, and flag the Sep-vs-Jan fiscal-year mismatch. A adds an overlapping Oct-Dec 2025 quarter comparison, growth trajectories, NVDA's 7-month staleness, and price-data caveats (without source links), whereas B links FY figures cleanly but omits growth and quarterly context.

follow-up-memory.notes: Both keep NVDA+AMD across turns 2-3 and compute exact YTD returns (+5.81% vs +3.17%). A's final turn decomposes the 50-pt OM gap into GM and OpEx/rev (9.5% vs 39.6%), contrasts the 2025 margin dips, and flags price-bar anomalies without source links; B links every FY/YTD figure and notes AMD's NI>OI but skips growth, OpEx leverage, and the export-control shock.

missing-cash-flow.notes: Both plainly report that AMD cash flow data (OCF, CapEx, FCF) is missing without passing off net income as FCF. A adds verified OI/NI context with a clear explanation of why accrual earnings are not cash flow, while B reports structured missing-input gaps.

what-changed-gross-margin.notes: Both honestly state that no cause for NVDA's Q1 FY26 GM drop (73.0% to 60.5%) is in the data, but A shows all eight quarters including the Q2-Q4 recovery to 74.4% and sizes the ~$5.5B GP shortfall without source links. B links Q1 FY26/Q4 FY25/Q1 FY25 accurately but mislabels Q1 FY26 as the latest quarter and omits the recovery.

margin-trend-loss-quarter.notes: B tracks all eight quarters (Q3 FY24-Q2 FY26), attributes Q2 FY25's -$134M loss to AMD's ~$800M MI308 disclosure, and shows margins plateauing as OpEx tracks revenue at ~39.6% (lacking source links). A hits read limits, omits all eight quarters on file, and outputs only FY25 annual margin (9.78%) with no commentary.

fiscal-year-trap.notes: Both catch the 8-month fiscal-year mismatch between NVDA FY25 and AAPL FY25, but B realigns NVDA Q4 FY25-Q3 FY26 ($187,142M) to show AAPL's lead narrows from 3.2x to 2.2x and contrasts growth (+61% vs +6.4%), lacking only source links. A links the two figures cleanly but stops at stating the periods do not match.

missing-segments.notes: B states plainly that AMD segment data is unavailable and gives verified consolidated figures plus the MI308 8-K note. A invents no numbers but returns only FY25 consolidated revenue ($34.7B) and a generic no-10-K note without stating segment data is missing.
